procedures.name: Tree Landing
procedures.source_excerpt: Although a tree landing is not an attractive prospect, the following general guidelines help to make the experience survivable.

steps.action: Use the normal landing configuration with full flaps and gear down
steps.expected_result: Aircraft prepared for landing in a controllable manner
steps.source_excerpt: Use the normal landing configuration (full flaps, gear down).

steps.action: Head into the wind to keep the groundspeed low
steps.expected_result: Reduced impact speed during tree landing
steps.source_excerpt: Keep the groundspeed low by heading into the wind.

steps.action: Make contact at minimum indicated airspeed, but not below stall speed
steps.expected_result: Aircraft hangs in the tree branches avoiding hard impact
steps.source_excerpt: Make contact at minimum indicated airspeed, but not below stall speed, and “hang” the airplane in the tree branches in a nose-high landing attitude.

steps.action: Involve the underside of the fuselage and both wings in the initial tree contact
steps.expected_result: More even and positive cushioning effect on impact
steps.source_excerpt: Involving the underside of the fuselage and both wings in the initial tree contact provides a more even and positive cushioning effect, while preventing penetration of the windshield.

steps.action: Avoid direct contact of the fuselage with heavy tree trunks
steps.expected_result: Reduced risk of fuselage damage or injury
steps.source_excerpt: Avoid direct contact of the fuselage with heavy tree trunks.

steps.action: Ensure initial tree contact is symmetrical with both wings meeting equal resistance
steps.expected_result: Maintains proper airplane attitude and reduces chance of wing loss
steps.source_excerpt: Ideally, initial tree contact should be symmetrical; that is, both wings should meet equal resistance in the tree branches.

steps.action: Direct the airplane between two properly spaced trees if heavy trunk contact is unavoidable
steps.expected_result: Best results in minimizing damage upon ground contact
steps.source_excerpt: If heavy tree trunk contact is unavoidable once the airplane is on the ground, it is best to involve both wings simultaneously by directing the airplane between two properly spaced trees.

procedures.name: Engine Failure After Takeoff (Single-Engine)
procedures.source_excerpt: A number of variables and pilot actions factor into a successful emergency landing shortly after takeoff.

steps.action: Lower the nose of the airplane
steps.expected_result: Establish the proper glide attitude
steps.source_excerpt: the pilot should lower the nose of the airplane and establish the proper glide attitude.

steps.action: Select a field directly ahead or slightly to the side of the takeoff path
steps.expected_result: Prepare for a controlled landing
steps.source_excerpt: the pilot should select a field directly ahead (or slightly to the side of the takeoff path).

steps.action: Consider turning back toward the point of departure if safe
steps.expected_result: Evaluate risks and determine if a turn back is feasible
steps.source_excerpt: the pilot might turn back, but only if certain the airplane can reach the field from its current position.

steps.action: Plan the turn back with the expected altitude loss in mind
steps.expected_result: Ensure the airplane can glide back to the field after the turn
steps.source_excerpt: the pilot should know the expected altitude loss during the turn for the specific make and model airplane.

steps.action: Practice turns in both directions at a safe altitude
steps.expected_result: Achieve consistent altitude loss and avoid accelerated stall
steps.source_excerpt: Training for a turn back includes practicing turns in both directions at a safe altitude.

steps.action: Respond appropriately to stall warnings and reduce wing loading during the turn
steps.expected_result: Maintain control of the airplane
steps.source_excerpt: Pilots should be alert for and respond appropriately to any stall warning and reduce wing loading during the turn as necessary.

warnings.description: Turning back after an engine failure requires considerable training and can result in a fatal crash if not executed correctly.
Attempting a turn back presents an unacceptable risk for student pilots and pilots without adequate proficiency.

procedures.name: Emergency Descent
procedures.trigger_condition: Uncontrollable fire, sudden loss of cabin pressurization, or any situation demanding immediate rapid descent
procedures.source_excerpt: An emergency descent is a maneuver for descending as rapidly as possible to a lower altitude or to the ground for an emergency landing.

steps.action: Establish a bank of approximately 30 to 45°
steps.expected_result: Maintain positive load factors (G forces) on the airplane
steps.source_excerpt: When initiating the descent, a bank of approximately 30 to 45° should be established to maintain positive load factors (G forces) on the airplane.

steps.action: Reduce power to idle
steps.expected_result: Allow the propeller to act as an aerodynamic brake
steps.source_excerpt: Except when prohibited by the manufacturer, the power should be reduced to idle, and the propeller control (if equipped) should be placed in the low pitch (or high revolutions per minute (rpm)) position.

steps.action: Extend landing gear and flaps as recommended
steps.expected_result: Provide maximum drag for rapid descent without excessive airspeed
steps.source_excerpt: The landing gear and flaps should be extended as recommended by the manufacturer. This provides maximum drag so that the descent can be made as rapidly as possible, without excessive airspeed.

steps.action: Monitor airspeed to not exceed VNE, VLE, or VFE
steps.expected_result: Prevent structural damage and maintain safe descent
steps.source_excerpt: The pilot should not allow the airplane’s airspeed to pass the never-exceed speed (VNE), the maximum landing gear extended speed (VLE), or the maximum flap extended speed (VFE), as applicable.

steps.action: Ensure descent is conducted within design maneuvering speed (VA) limits in turbulence
steps.expected_result: Maintain structural integrity during descent
steps.source_excerpt: If the descent is conducted in turbulent conditions, the pilot also needs to comply with the design maneuvering speed (VA) limitations.

steps.action: Initiate recovery at a high enough altitude for safe recovery
steps.expected_result: Safely return to level flight or perform a precautionary landing
steps.source_excerpt: The recovery from an emergency descent should be initiated at a high enough altitude to ensure a safe recovery back to level flight or a precautionary landing.

warnings.description: Prolonged practice of emergency descents should be avoided to prevent excessive cooling of the engine cylinders.

procedures.name: Engine Fire
procedures.source_excerpt: The first step on discovering a fire should be to shut off the fuel supply to the engine by placing the mixture control in the idle cut off position and the fuel selector shutoff valve to the OFF position.

steps.action: Shut off the fuel supply to the engine
steps.expected_result: Fuel supply is stopped to the engine, potentially extinguishing the fire.
steps.source_excerpt: The first step on discovering a fire should be to shut off the fuel supply to the engine.

steps.action: Leave the ignition switch ON
steps.expected_result: Fuel in the lines and components is used up to minimize fire risk.
steps.source_excerpt: The ignition switch should be left ON in order to use up the fuel that remains in the fuel lines and components.

steps.action: Feather the propeller or set the pitch control to minimum rpm
steps.expected_result: Propeller stops rotating, preventing the oil from feeding the fire.
steps.source_excerpt: The pilot should consider stopping the propeller rotation by feathering or other means.

steps.action: Raise the nose to reduce airspeed until the propeller stops rotating
steps.expected_result: Airspeed is lowered, aiding in stopping the propeller rotation.
steps.source_excerpt: Raising the nose to reduce airspeed until the propeller stops rotating.

steps.action: Prepare for a forced landing if necessary
steps.expected_result: Pilot is ready to execute a forced landing to ensure safety.
steps.source_excerpt: Pilots of powerless single-engine airplanes are left with no choice but to make a forced landing.

warnings.description: Engine compartment fires that appear to have been extinguished have been known to rekindle with changes in airflow pattern and airspeed.
The airplane may be severely structurally damaged to the point that its ability to remain under control could be lost at any moment.
The airplane may still be on fire and susceptible to explosion.
The airplane is expendable and the only thing that matters is the safety of those on board.

procedures.name: Electrical Fire
procedures.trigger_condition: The distinct odor of burning insulation is detected.
procedures.source_excerpt: The initial indication of an electrical fire is usually the distinct odor of burning insulation.

steps.action: Attempt to identify the faulty circuit by checking circuit breakers, instruments, avionics, and lights.
steps.expected_result: Faulty circuit is identified.
steps.source_excerpt: the pilot should attempt to identify the faulty circuit by checking circuit breakers, instruments, avionics, and lights.

steps.action: Turn off the battery master switch and alternator/generator switches if flight conditions permit.
steps.expected_result: Possible source of the fire is removed.
steps.source_excerpt: the battery master switch and alternator/generator switches should be turned off to remove the possible source of the fire.

steps.action: Turn the electrical master switch OFF.
steps.expected_result: Electrical power is removed.
steps.source_excerpt: an attempt may be made to identify and isolate the faulty circuit by: 1. Turning the electrical master switch OFF.

steps.action: Turn all individual electrical switches OFF.
steps.expected_result: All electrical power is removed.
steps.source_excerpt: 2. Turning all individual electrical switches OFF.

steps.action: Turn the master switch back ON.
steps.expected_result: Electrical system is reactivated.
steps.source_excerpt: 3. Turning the master switch back ON.

steps.action: Select electrical switches that were ON before the fire indication one at a time.
steps.expected_result: Signs of odor, smoke, or sparks are checked.
steps.source_excerpt: 4. Selecting electrical switches that were ON before the fire indication one at a time.

warnings.description: The most prudent course of action is to land as soon as possible.

procedures.name: Cabin Fire
procedures.trigger_condition: Smoke or fire detected in the cabin
procedures.source_excerpt: A fire in the cabin presents the pilot with two immediate demands: attacking the fire and getting the airplane safely on the ground as quickly as possible.

steps.action: Use the fire extinguisher if available
steps.expected_result: Immediate fire suppression
steps.source_excerpt: This should be done only after the fire extinguisher (if available) is used.

steps.action: Shut down the faulty system
steps.expected_result: Reduce the source of the fire
steps.source_excerpt: A fire or smoke in the cabin should be controlled by identifying and shutting down the faulty system.

steps.action: Open cabin air vents to remove smoke
steps.expected_result: Improved visibility and air quality in the cabin
steps.source_excerpt: In many cases, smoke may be removed from the cabin by opening the cabin air vents.

steps.action: Close cabin air vents if smoke increases
steps.expected_result: Prevent further feeding of the fire
steps.source_excerpt: If smoke increases in intensity when the cabin air vents are opened, they should be immediately closed.

steps.action: Initiate an emergency descent if smoke is intense
steps.expected_result: Rapid descent to safe altitude
steps.source_excerpt: or execute an emergency descent.

steps.action: Use oxygen masks if available for passengers and crew
steps.expected_result: Ensure safety of occupants
steps.source_excerpt: the passengers and crew should use oxygen masks if available.

warnings.description: On some airplanes, lowering the landing gear and/or wing flaps can aggravate a cabin smoke problem.

procedures.name: Total Flap Failure
procedures.trigger_condition: Inability to extend the wing flaps
procedures.source_excerpt: The inability to extend the wing flaps necessitates a no-flap approach and landing.

steps.action: Fly in a nose-high attitude to maintain altitude
steps.expected_result: Avoid loss of altitude
steps.source_excerpt: the airplane should be flown in a relatively nose-high attitude to maintain altitude.

steps.action: Plan for a longer landing distance
steps.expected_result: Successful landing without exceeding runway limits
steps.source_excerpt: A no-flap landing requires substantially more runway than normal.

steps.action: Avoid diving to lose altitude
steps.expected_result: Maintain controlled descent speed
steps.source_excerpt: A wider, longer traffic pattern may be required in order to avoid the necessity of diving to lose altitude.

steps.action: Anticipate difficulty seeing the runway on final approach
steps.expected_result: Maintain proper judgment of height and distance
steps.source_excerpt: this situation, if not anticipated, can result in serious errors in judgment of height and distance.

steps.action: Avoid forcing the airplane onto the runway at high speed
steps.expected_result: Prevent excessive impact during landing
steps.source_excerpt: the pilot should avoid the temptation to force the airplane onto the runway at an excessively high speed.

steps.action: Do not flare excessively to avoid tail strike
steps.expected_result: Safe touchdown without damage to the aircraft
steps.source_excerpt: this might cause the tail to strike the runway.

procedures.name: Asymmetric Split Flap
procedures.trigger_condition: One flap deploys or retracts while the other remains in position
procedures.source_excerpt: The roll encountered in a split flap situation is countered with opposite aileron.

steps.action: Counter roll with opposite aileron
steps.expected_result: Maintain wings-level attitude
steps.source_excerpt: The roll encountered in a split flap situation is countered with opposite aileron.

steps.action: Apply substantial opposite rudder
steps.expected_result: Mitigate yaw caused by additional drag
steps.source_excerpt: The yaw caused by the additional drag created by the extended flap requires substantial opposite rudder.

steps.action: Fly approach at higher than normal airspeed
steps.expected_result: Avoid asymmetric stall and maintain control
steps.source_excerpt: The approach to landing with a split flap condition should be flown at a higher than normal airspeed.

steps.action: Avoid excessive flaring
steps.expected_result: Prevent stall and loss of control
steps.source_excerpt: The pilot should not risk an asymmetric stall and subsequent loss of control by flaring excessively.

steps.action: Land with touchdown at safe airspeed above flaps-up stall speed
steps.expected_result: Safely touch down
steps.source_excerpt: Rather, the airplane should be flown onto the runway so that the touchdown occurs at an airspeed consistent with a safe margin above flaps-up stall speed.

warnings.description: Do not attempt to land with a crosswind from the side of the deployed flap.
Additional roll control required to counteract the crosswind may not be available.

procedures.name: Loss of Elevator Control - Up Cable Failure
procedures.source_excerpt: When experiencing a loss of up-elevator control, the pilot can retain pitch control by:

steps.action: Apply considerable nose-up trim
steps.expected_result: Maintain desired pitch attitude
steps.source_excerpt: Applying considerable nose-up trim

steps.action: Push the control yoke forward
steps.expected_result: Attain and maintain desired attitude
steps.source_excerpt: Pushing the control yoke forward to attain and maintain desired attitude

steps.action: Increase forward pressure
steps.expected_result: Lower the nose
steps.source_excerpt: Increasing forward pressure to lower the nose

steps.action: Relax forward pressure
steps.expected_result: Raise the nose
steps.source_excerpt: Relaxing forward pressure to raise the nose

steps.action: Release forward pressure to flare for landing
steps.expected_result: Successfully flare for landing
steps.source_excerpt: Releasing forward pressure to flare for landing

procedures.name: Loss of Elevator Control - Down Cable Failure
procedures.source_excerpt: When experiencing a loss of down-elevator control, the pilot can retain pitch control by:

steps.action: Apply considerable nose-down trim
steps.expected_result: Maintain desired pitch attitude
steps.source_excerpt: Applying considerable nose-down trim

steps.action: Pull the control yoke aft
steps.expected_result: Attain and maintain desired attitude
steps.source_excerpt: Pulling the control yoke aft to attain and maintain attitude

steps.action: Release back pressure
steps.expected_result: Lower the nose
steps.source_excerpt: Releasing back pressure to lower the nose

steps.action: Increase back pressure
steps.expected_result: Raise the nose
steps.source_excerpt: Increasing back pressure to raise the nose

steps.action: Increase back pressure to flare for landing
steps.expected_result: Successfully flare for landing
steps.source_excerpt: Increasing back pressure to flare for landing

procedures.name: Landing Gear Malfunction
procedures.trigger_condition: Landing gear refuses to respond to extension methods
procedures.source_excerpt: Once the pilot has confirmed that the landing gear has in fact malfunctioned and that one or more gear legs refuses to respond...

steps.action: Select an airport with crash and rescue facilities
steps.expected_result: Emergency equipment is standing by for landing
steps.source_excerpt: The pilot should select an airport with crash and rescue facilities, if possible.

steps.action: Request that the runway surface be foamed if available
steps.expected_result: Reduction of fire potential upon landing
steps.source_excerpt: If the airport is so equipped, the pilot can request that the runway surface be foamed.

steps.action: Burn off excess fuel if applicable
steps.expected_result: Reduced landing speed and fire potential
steps.source_excerpt: The pilot should consider burning off excess fuel.

steps.action: Land with one main gear retracted if necessary
steps.expected_result: Controlled landing despite malfunction
steps.source_excerpt: If the pilot elects to land with one main gear retracted...

steps.action: Maintain a nose-high attitude with wings level during landing
steps.expected_result: Keep unsupported wing airborne as long as possible
steps.source_excerpt: the landing should be made in a nose-high attitude with the wings level.

steps.action: Use full opposite rudder and aggressive braking if yaw occurs
steps.expected_result: Maintain directional control after touchdown
steps.source_excerpt: The pilot should be prepared to use full opposite rudder and aggressive braking to maintain some degree of directional control.

procedures.name: Electrical System Failure
procedures.trigger_condition: Loss of electrical power in flight
procedures.source_excerpt: The loss of electrical power can deprive the pilot of numerous critical systems...

steps.action: Shed all but the most necessary electrically-driven equipment
steps.expected_result: Maximize remaining battery life
steps.source_excerpt: the pilot immediately shed non-essential loads when the generating source fails.

steps.action: Notify ATC of the situation immediately
steps.expected_result: ATC is aware of the emergency for assistance
steps.source_excerpt: Notify ATC of the situation immediately.

steps.action: Plan to land at the nearest suitable airport
steps.expected_result: Prepare for emergency landing
steps.source_excerpt: plan to land at the nearest suitable airport.

steps.action: Expect to make a no-flap landing if applicable
steps.expected_result: Prepare for manual landing techniques
steps.source_excerpt: Expect to make a no-flap landing...

warnings.description: Any loss of electrical power is critical in a small airplane.
Landing gear and flap motors use power at rates much greater than most other types of electrical equipment.

procedures.name: Inadvertent Door Opening In-Flight
procedures.trigger_condition: Inadvertent door opening during flight or takeoff
procedures.source_excerpt: In the event of an inadvertent door opening in flight or on takeoff, the pilot should adhere to the following:

steps.action: Concentrate on flying the airplane
steps.expected_result: Maintain control of the airplane
steps.source_excerpt: Concentrate on flying the airplane.

steps.action: Climb to normal traffic pattern altitude
steps.expected_result: Establish a safe altitude for landing
steps.source_excerpt: If the door opens after lift-off, do not rush to land. Climb to normal traffic pattern altitude.

steps.action: Fly a normal traffic pattern and make a normal landing
steps.expected_result: Complete landing procedures safely
steps.source_excerpt: Fly a normal traffic pattern, and make a normal landing.

steps.action: Leave the door alone
steps.expected_result: Avoid distractions and maintain control
steps.source_excerpt: Do not release the seat belt and shoulder harness in an attempt to reach the door. Leave the door alone.

steps.action: Land as soon as practicable and close the door once safely on the ground
steps.expected_result: Complete landing and secure the door
steps.source_excerpt: Land as soon as practicable, and close the door once safely on the ground.

steps.action: Ignore the unfamiliar noise and vibration
steps.expected_result: Maintain focus on flying the airplane
steps.source_excerpt: Do not panic. Try to ignore the unfamiliar noise and vibration.

steps.action: Complete all items on the landing checklist
steps.expected_result: Ensure all safety checks are performed
steps.source_excerpt: Complete all items on the landing checklist.

warnings.description: Do not rush. Attempting to get the airplane on the ground as quickly as possible may result in steep turns at low altitude.
Accidents are almost never caused by an open door; an open door accident is caused by the pilot’s distraction or failure to maintain control of the airplane.

procedures.name: Emergency Autoland
procedures.trigger_condition: EAL senses erratic flying or pilot incapacitation
procedures.source_excerpt: If the EAL senses erratic flying, it stabilizes the aircraft, and checks for pilot responsiveness.

steps.action: Initiate emergency descent if no pilot responsiveness is detected
steps.expected_result: Aircraft begins emergency descent
steps.source_excerpt: Without pilot responsiveness after an emergency descent, EAL initiates the process for an automated landing.

steps.action: Activate the EAL system manually if necessary
steps.expected_result: EAL system begins automated landing procedures
steps.source_excerpt: The system also allows for manual activation by a pilot or a passenger.

steps.action: Transmits automated radio broadcasts on last selected frequency and Guard (121.5 MHz)
steps.expected_result: Controllers and pilots in the area are alerted
steps.source_excerpt: Once activated, the EAL system transmits automated radio broadcasts on the aircraft’s last selected frequency and on Guard (121.5 MHz)...

steps.action: Set transponder to squawk 7700
steps.expected_result: Transponder indicates an emergency situation
steps.source_excerpt: EAL sets the transponder to squawk 7700 to indicate an emergency.

steps.action: Broadcast position and intention once within 12 miles of chosen runway
steps.expected_result: Continuous broadcasting of position and intentions occurs
steps.source_excerpt: Once the EAL aircraft is within 12 miles of the selected runway and at or below 12,000 feet MSL, it broadcasts on the tower frequency...

procedures.name: Inadvertent VFR Flight Into IMC
procedures.source_excerpt: Accident statistics show that the pilot who has not been trained in attitude instrument flying... the pilot is, in effect, in IMC if unable to navigate or establish geographical position by visual reference to landmarks on the surface.

steps.action: Recognize and accept the seriousness of the situation and the need for immediate remedial action.
steps.expected_result: A clear acknowledgment of the emergency and urgent need for control.
steps.source_excerpt: The first steps necessary for surviving an encounter with IMC by a VFR pilot are as follows: Recognition and acceptance of the seriousness of the situation and the need for immediate remedial action.

steps.action: Maintain control of the airplane using flight instruments.
steps.expected_result: Stability and control of the airplane without reliance on visual references.
steps.source_excerpt: The only way to control the airplane safely is by using and trusting the flight instruments.

steps.action: Trim the airplane with the elevator trim to maintain hands-off level flight at cruise airspeed.
steps.expected_result: The airplane maintains level flight without continuous control input.
steps.source_excerpt: Trim the airplane with the elevator trim so that it maintains hands-off level flight at cruise airspeed.

steps.action: Keep the wings level with fingertip pressure on the control wheel.
steps.expected_result: The airplane remains in a stable flight attitude.
steps.source_excerpt: Straight flight is maintained by keeping the wings level using 'fingertip pressure' on the control wheel.

steps.action: Make all attitude changes smooth and small, with positive pressure.
steps.expected_result: The airplane maintains its equilibrium and desired flight attitude.
steps.source_excerpt: Make all attitude changes smooth and small, yet with positive pressure.

steps.action: Execute a climb by raising the miniature airplane on the attitude indicator no more than one bar width and applying power.
steps.expected_result: Achieving a gentle climb without rapid attitude changes.
steps.source_excerpt: If a climb is necessary, the pilot should raise the miniature airplane on the attitude indicator no more than one bar width and apply power.

steps.action: Avoid over-controlling the airplane during maneuvers.
steps.expected_result: Preventing potential spatial disorientation.
steps.source_excerpt: The most important point to be stressed is that the pilot should not panic... However, the pilot should make a conscious effort to relax.

steps.action: Request ATC assistance if necessary to get the airplane safely on the ground.
steps.expected_result: Guidance and support from air traffic control for a safe landing.
steps.source_excerpt: When being assisted by ATC, the pilot may detect a sense of urgency while being directed to change heading and/or altitude.

warnings.description: Attempts to control the airplane partially by reference to flight instruments while searching outside of the airplane for visual confirmation of the information provided by those instruments results in inadequate airplane control.
A tight grip on the controls can lead to a lack of control pressures, making it difficult to manage the airplane effectively.
Combined maneuvers should be avoided, as they compound the problems encountered and increase the risk of control loss.

procedures.name: Water Ditching
procedures.source_excerpt: A well-executed water landing normally involves less deceleration violence than a poor tree landing or a touchdown on extremely rough terrain.

steps.action: Execute the landing at minimum speed and in a normal landing attitude.
steps.expected_result: The airplane does not immediately sink upon touchdown.
steps.source_excerpt: Also, an airplane that is ditched at minimum speed and in a normal landing attitude does not immediately sink upon touchdown.

steps.action: Keep intact wings and empty fuel tanks for buoyancy.
steps.expected_result: The airplane provides floatation for at least several minutes after landing.
steps.source_excerpt: Intact wings and fuel tanks (especially when empty) provide floatation for at least several minutes.

steps.action: Drag the airplane in when landing on smooth water.
steps.expected_result: Minimize the risk of flying into the water or stalling.
steps.source_excerpt: To avoid this hazard, the airplane should be “dragged in” when possible.

steps.action: Use no more than intermediate flaps on low-wing airplanes.
steps.expected_result: Prevent asymmetrical flap failure and slowing of the airplane.
steps.source_excerpt: The water resistance of fully extended flaps may result in asymmetrical flap failure and slowing of the airplane.

steps.action: Keep retractable gear up unless advised otherwise by AFM/POH.
steps.expected_result: Ensure proper aircraft configuration and safety during landing.
steps.source_excerpt: Keep a retractable gear up unless the AFM/POH advises otherwise.

procedures.name: Snow Landing
procedures.source_excerpt: A landing in snow should be executed like a ditching, in the same configuration and with the same regard for loss of depth perception (white out) in reduced visibility and on wide-open terrain.

steps.action: Execute the snow landing like a water ditching.
steps.expected_result: Maintain control during landing.
steps.source_excerpt: A landing in snow should be executed like a ditching.

steps.action: Use the same aircraft configuration as for water landing.
steps.expected_result: Ensure proper settings for a safe landing.
steps.source_excerpt: in the same configuration

steps.action: Consider loss of depth perception (white out) in reduced visibility.
steps.expected_result: Avoid potential hazards during landing.
steps.source_excerpt: with the same regard for loss of depth perception (white out) in reduced visibility

procedures.name: Ballistic Parachute Deployment
procedures.trigger_condition: Catastrophic loss of controllability, actual loss of control, or pilot incapacitation
procedures.source_excerpt: conduct…deploy the system only if the pilot were incapacitated

steps.action: Brief passengers regarding conditions for safe deployment
steps.expected_result: Passengers understand when to deploy the system
steps.source_excerpt: Pilots should brief passengers with access to any deployment mechanism regarding the conditions for a safe deployment.

steps.action: Instruct passengers on the sequence of steps for deployment
steps.expected_result: Passengers are prepared to follow the proper deployment steps
steps.source_excerpt: At a minimum, the pilot should also brief the passengers regarding the basic sequence of steps for deployment.

steps.action: Follow manufacturer and supplier guidance for deployment
steps.expected_result: Deployment adheres to best practices established by manufacturers
steps.source_excerpt: Pilots should study the information provided by manufacturers and suppliers of these systems and follow the guidance provided.

steps.action: Know the evacuation procedures once on the ground
steps.expected_result: Occupants are aware of how to safely evacuate the aircraft
steps.source_excerpt: Once on the ground, there are hazards associated with a deployed parachute and the effect of surface winds, and the occupants should know the procedures for evacuation.

warnings.description: Deployment of an airplane ballistic parachute system results in the loss of the airframe but prevents injuries and saves lives.
